You cross the grating to the workbench, boots ringing softly under the strip lights. The woman sets her wrench down and turns, brass-rimmed ports catching the instrument glow. “Mara Venn,” she says. Her gaze shifts to the orchid beneath the clear mat as you ask who left it there.

“I don’t know.” She draws the frayed scarf tighter at her throat, then picks up the wrench and returns to the coupling. A bead of hydraulic fluid runs from the joint onto the bench; beyond the bay door, the irregular tapping stops.

turns.narration:
You lift the clear mat’s edge and turn the orchid beneath the strip lights. Its brittle stem leaves a faint smear of dark oil on your glove; along one petal, a clean crescent of adhesive clings to the surface. Your thumb catches the mat’s sharp edge, splitting the glove at the seam.

You follow the hydraulic bead across the cold workbench to the coupling Mara tightened. Fluid wells from a hairline split beneath its collar. Mara stops with the wrench in hand as another person steps out from behind the cargo crates: a narrow-shouldered dockhand with a strip of matching adhesive stuck to one cuff. They glance at the orchid, then at the split coupling. “That joint was sound before she touched it,” Mara says, and lowers the wrench without looking away from the newcomer.

The dockhand backs toward the sealed bay door. Your torn glove shines with hydraulic fluid, and the orchid’s dark smear marks the torn seam; behind you, Mara’s coupling continues to leak onto the workbench.

judge.weakness: Slack is omitted while an unnamed dockhand takes the scene’s role.

turns.narration:
You lunge across the workbench and clamp your torn, fluid-slick glove over the split coupling, bracing your other hand against the metal. The leak dwindles to a thin seep beneath your palm. Slack darts for the sealed bay door, but you plant your shoulder across the narrow gap and stop him short. His adhesive-marked cuff snags on a bench bracket; a slim access badge slips free and skids across the grating.

A magnetic shudder runs through the docking bay. The strip lights flicker, and comms crackle into static before cutting out. Slack freezes with one hand raised, eyes fixed on your grip over the damaged line. Mara sets down her wrench and keeps clear of the leaking joint. “Hold that,” she says. “I’ll isolate the feed.” She turns to the control panel while the badge lies near Slack’s boot, its marked edge turned toward you.

The coupling remains damaged, and your split glove darkens with fluid, but the bay door stays sealed and the leak is under your hand. Slack’s gaze shifts from the badge to the door controls; Mara reaches for the isolation switch, leaving you the choice between the dockhand and the failing line.

judge.weakness: The magnetic shudder and comms failure add a serious complication despite the strong hit.

turns.narration:
Your palm stays clamped over the split coupling. Hydraulic fluid slicks the torn glove, and the metal presses hard into the heel of your hand. You ask Mara whether the isolation switch will stop the leak without venting the bay. She reaches the panel and throws the switch; the line bucks against your grip, then the flow dwindles to a seep. “It should stop the leak without venting the bay,” she says. “Keep your hand there. That collar can cut through the glove.” The pressure eases, but the glove’s torn seam widens beneath the coupling.

You ask Slack why he reached for the sealed bay door and what his badge opens, keeping your eyes on him. He glances at the badge near his boot, then tests the gap beside your shoulder. “It opens the maintenance lock. I was trying to get out before you searched me.” He nudges the badge toward you with his toe. “Take it, and don’t look in the badge log.” Mara keeps one hand on the isolation switch; behind Slack, the sealed door’s status strip flickers twice, and the magnetic vibration returns through the grating.

turns.narration:
You release the coupling only after Mara slides a clamp over the split and cinches it tight; the hydraulic seep stops. “Isolation’s still engaged,” she says, keeping her hand on the switch. “That glove won’t hold pressure much longer.” The badge lies within reach beside Slack’s boot.

You snatch it and drive your shoulder into the sealed bay door as the magnetic vibration surges through the grating. The door shudders against you but stays shut. Its status strip flickers through a repeating sequence: access granted, then lock retained. The impact catches you in the side; blood wells through torn fabric and darkens your shirt. Slack keeps his hands raised. “Don’t check the log. I came here because the door’s maintenance lock showed an open-cycle warning.” Mara watches the badge in your hand, then the strip. “The log will show which credential triggered that cycle,” she says, and turns back to the panel. The vibration continues beneath your braced shoulder while the badge’s display wakes in your palm.

turns.action: I brace my injured side against the grating and wrench the sealed bay door’s man
turns.narration:
You brace your injured side against the grating and wrench Slack’s badge into the manual release as the vibration surges. Pain cuts across your ribs. The badge bends between your fingers; the lock stays engaged. The door does not move. A hard pressure pulse hits the sealed bay, and the panel flashes red as its status strip drops dark. The vibration deepens beneath your boots, steady enough to rattle the tools on Mara’s bench.

Mara keeps the pressure controls stable, one hand firm on the isolation panel. Slack watches the badge in your grip. “The warning named service credential K-17,” he says. “Check the hatch-cycle entry.” Mara pulls the access log onto the panel. “K-17 logged a manual purge-valve test six minutes before the orchid was found. That proves the credential was used, not who used it.” She turns toward your bloodied side and holds out a compression wrap. “I can bind that while the pressure holds. Your call.” The door remains sealed; a fresh pulse makes the panel’s dead display shiver against its frame.

For a moment, the bay holds only the reactor hum and the rasp of your breathing. The wrap stays in Mara’s open hand, and Slack stands between you and the locked door, eyes fixed on the badge.

judge.weakness: The failed attempt still yields a useful access-log clue, giving the MISS a silver lining.

You snatch the compression wrap from Mara and cinch it hard around your ribs. The pressure bites through the bruising; your breath catches against the tight band. Mara keeps one hand on the control panel, jaw clenched as she holds the isolation feed. “I can’t hold this and help you at the door,” she says.

You drive your shoulder into the manual release. The panel gives a blunt jolt through your collarbone, but the mechanism stays locked. Before you can strike again, the next pressure pulse hits. The sealed door bows inward a fraction; a seam spits hydraulic mist across the grating, and the panel’s dark display rattles loose at one corner. Mara’s control hand slips. She catches the switch before it moves, then stares at you, anger tight in her face. “You’ve made the seal worse.” Slack bolts for the far service passage, snatching up a loose tool roll as he goes; his flight leaves the K-17 access trail untouched and out of reach. Beyond the door, metal grinds under the rising pressure, and the next pulse is already building through the deck.

turns.action: ## I wanted to talk to them, not confront them
turns.narration:
Night presses cold beyond the docking bay’s narrow ports. You keep your hands away from the dead panel and the sealed door, the compression wrap tight around your ribs. “I wanted to talk to Mara Venn, not confront her.” Your voice carries over the reactor hum and the faint hiss of the damaged seal.

Mara holds the isolation control, shoulders tense from keeping pressure steady. She looks from your face to the wrap. “Understood. I can bind that injury while I maintain the controls.” She offers the wrap again, practical and brief. Slack stays near the service passage, guarded eyes flicking toward the K-17 log. “I can show you who had access to that credential,” he says. “That won’t prove who used it.” A thin shiver passes through the grating; the dark panel rattles against its frame, and Mara’s fingers tighten on the control. The wrap remains in her hand, the log open, and Slack waits by the passage.
